bug_semantics: A browser page on an attacker-controlled DNS name can rebind that same origin to the victim's loopback Paperclip server. Because Paperclip did not reject the attacker's Host header and the default local-trusted behavior treated requests without credentials as an instance-admin board actor, the page could create a company and a process-adapter agent with attacker-controlled command/args, then invoke the agent heartbeat/wakeup route; the server passed that configuration to child_process.spawn as the Paperclip OS user, yielding drive-by command execution.
flaw_origin: abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b is the first commit that completed the exploitable mechanism: it mounted an actor middleware which assigned every unauthenticated request a board actor, added board-accessible company/agent creation and heartbeat invocation routes, and added the process execution service that spawned attacker-controlled command and args, all without Host validation. The parent had only CRUD agent routes and no auth middleware, heartbeat service, invocation route, or command sink. e1f2be7ecff711f2f5db9a0f64dbd3133df4410e later named/defaulted the same implicit-admin behavior as local_trusted; 85c0b9a3dc3795bf33646ef128ad070181c7abec later added a hostname guard but enabled it only for authenticated/private deployments, preserving the already-existing local-trusted flaw rather than introducing it.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/security/advisories/GHSA-x8hx-rhr2-9rf7 describes the same-origin DNS-rebinding sequence, implicit local_trusted instance-admin actor, disabled hostname guard, process-adapter spawn, and create/import-then-wakeup attack. In the validated clone, `git show abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b -- server/src/app.ts server/src/middleware/auth.ts server/src/routes/companies.ts server/src/routes/agents.ts server/src/services/heartbeat.ts` shows app.use(actorMiddleware(db)); middleware default `req.actor = { type: "board", userId: "board" }`; POST /api/companies, POST /api/companies/:companyId/agents, POST /api/agents/:id/heartbeat/invoke; and executeProcessRun reading config.command/config.args and calling spawn(command, args, ...). At that tree packages/shared/src/validators/agent.ts permits client-controlled adapterType (default process) and arbitrary adapterConfig. `git log -L 106,170:server/src/services/heartbeat.ts abadd...` and `git log -L 12,16:server/src/middleware/auth.ts abadd...` both terminate at abadd; `git log -S'executeProcessRun' -- server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`, `-S'heartbeat/invoke' -- server/src/routes/agents.ts`, and `-S'req.actor = { type: "board", userId: "board" }' -- server/src/middleware/auth.ts` also identify abadd as the addition (later 47ccd... only extracts/moves the process adapter). Direct parent verification: `git cat-file -e 8c830eae70a14723749828f0ce5d9ae435270e9c:server/src/middleware/auth.ts` and the analogous heartbeat.ts check both fail because the paths do not exist, while `git show 8c830...:server/src/routes/agents.ts` contains CRUD only and no invoke/execution route. `git cat-file commit abadd...` gives raw author and committer Forgotten <forgottenrunes@protonmail.com> and the exact Claude trailer quoted in ai_marker; the commit is a normal one-parent commit, not a merge/release/refactor/squash artifact. `git show 32a9165ddf6308f3b46eae0653b6f583e502e538 -- server/src/app.ts server/src/__tests__/app-private-hostname-gate.test.ts` shows the direct close: it replaces `deploymentMode === "authenticated" && deploymentExposure === "private"` with a private-exposure predicate covering both local_trusted and authenticated, with all four mode/exposure cases tested. Its parent is 50cd76d8a3f2fc06d1a5af63840abd3d7a1bcd02 and still has the vulnerable authenticated-only gate. Release ancestry: `git tag --contains abadd... --list 'v*'` starts with v0.3.0; peeled commits are v0.3.0=7e8908afa23d3c89558e4cd96ef2aa85692e447d and v0.3.1=63c62e3ada077bac45292f3d2779bd48a8831cda, and both contain the BIC but not the fix. v2026.403.0=a07237779bd5391a4683a754ed95249d57a49b2c still shows the authenticated-only gate; v2026.416.0=b8725c52eff66cdea8cb223f1ca885475a254468 is the first v* tag containing 32a9165... and shows local_trusted included. Thus repository history proves v0.3.1 remained vulnerable and v2026.416.0 is the first fixed tagged release, despite the syndicated `<0.3.1` range and the first-party page's simultaneous `Patched versions: None` metadata.
reasoning: The causal unit is not the later hostname-guard commit: local drive-by RCE already existed. The initial API-server commit c9d7cbfe4489bb1506c596a4c3a64b184969b548 exposed CRUD but lacked command execution. abadd469bc85e9fa5137ff5ffce433f1c2db2c0b then simultaneously made credentialless requests authoritative board requests and added attacker-configurable process execution reachable through an API invoke route, with no Host check, so it is the smallest commit after which DNS rebinding could achieve OS command execution. Its direct parent lacks every completing element, proving parent absence. Later commits renamed the trust model to default local_trusted, added company import as an alternate provisioning route, and partially protected authenticated/private mode, but those are persistence/attack-convenience changes rather than the BIC. Commit 32a9165ddf6308f3b46eae0653b6f583e502e538 directly closes the missing Host-boundary check for private local_trusted deployments and is first released in v2026.416.0. Because the BIC commit object itself explicitly co-authors Claude Opus 4.6 and that BIC first wrote the flawed mechanism, the protocol verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE; AI disclosures on later commits, including the fix, are irrelevant.
